newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: London coffee seen challenging US$2,100 resistance.
newsitem.headline: London coffee seen challenging US$2,100 resistance.

text.p: London robusta futures are tipped to open US$20-$30 higher later on Thursday, threatening to soar past resistance at $2,100 a tonne, as the market plays catch-up with the New York arabica market, traders said.
"The due is at least $30 higher, but that means we will have to break the $2,100 barrier and London has so far failed to break that level," a dealer for a European trading house said.
"It has to break strong resistance at $2,100. We're very close to it though," he added, referring to Wednesday's close on London's key July robusta contract at $2,090.
Another dealer said the July contract should open $20-$30 higher. "It's trying to catch up with New York so it should move up purely on the numbers," he said.

July arabicas in New York climbed more than five percent on the day to end on Wednesday at 253.10 U.S. cents a lb following news the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC), meeting in London, had extended coffee export quotas for another 12 months.
While initially providing a boost to the market, Asian coffee dealers dismissed the decision of the 14-member ACPC to extend export quotas.
"Everybody cheats in the ACPC at some point so who will believe these quotas," a dealer said.
"This is nice talk, but has anybody followed it? Do you think sellers will hold back with prices at these levels?" another asked. "I don't think this organisation has any influence in the market."
